connections.explanation: Fleeing Saul, David asks the priest at Nob for bread, and the priest gives him the holy bread from before the LORD. When his disciples are criticised for plucking grain on the Sabbath, Jesus asks whether they have not read what David did when he was hungry; the Greek for the bread of the Presence is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.excerpt: Then David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no man with you?”

ends.sectionTitle: The Disciples Called; Sermon on the Plain
ends.excerpt: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,

connections.label: Saul the son of Kish
connections.explanation: Samuel anoints Saul with oil as prince over the LORD's inheritance. Retelling Israel's story at Pisidian Antioch, Paul says the people asked for a king and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin.

ends.excerpt: Then Samuel took the vial of oil and poured it on his head, then kissed him and said, “Hasn’t the LORD anointed you to be prince over his inheritance?
Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

connections.label: A man after my heart
connections.explanation: When Saul disobeys, Samuel tells him that the LORD has sought a man after his own heart to lead his people. Paul, in the same sermon, says God raised up David as king and testified that he had found in David a man after his heart (the Greek for heart below).

ends.excerpt: But now your kingdom will not continue. The LORD has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept that which…
When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

connections.label: Better than burnt offerings
connections.explanation: Samuel tells Saul that the LORD delights more in obedience than in burnt offerings and sacrifices. The scribe who questions Jesus says that loving God and neighbour is more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices, with the Septuagint's rare word for whole burnt offerings (below).

ends.excerpt: Samuel said, “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the LORD’s voice? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Questions in the Temple
ends.excerpt: and to love him with all the heart, with all the understanding, all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and…

connections.label: Not by appearance
connections.explanation: When Samuel looks at Jesse's eldest son, the LORD tells him that people look at the outward appearance but the LORD looks at the heart. Jesus tells the crowd at the Feast of Booths not to judge by appearance but with right judgement; his word for appearance is the Septuagint's in 1 Samuel 16:7 (below).

ends.excerpt: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD…
Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” Therefore some of them of Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this he whom they seek to kill?

connections.label: Across the brook Kidron
connections.explanation: Fleeing from Absalom, David crosses the brook Kidron toward the wilderness while all the country weeps. John says that after his last discourse Jesus went out with his disciples across the brook Kidron to a garden, with the Septuagint's word for a winter brook, found nowhere else in the New Testament (below).

ends.excerpt: All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.
When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.

connections.label: He went away and hanged himself
connections.explanation: When his counsel is not followed, Ahithophel, who had betrayed David to join Absalom, goes home and hangs himself. Matthew says Judas threw down the silver and went away and hanged himself, using the Septuagint's verb from Ahithophel's death, found nowhere else in the New Testament (below).

ends.excerpt: When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey, arose, and went home to his city, set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of…
He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary and departed. Then he went away and hanged himself.

connections.label: Praise among the nations
connections.explanation: David's song of deliverance ends with his vow to give thanks to the LORD among the nations and sing praises to his name. Paul quotes it as written to show that the Gentiles too would glorify God for his mercy, in the Septuagint's words (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Last Things: Famine, Song, Heroes, Census
ends.excerpt: Therefore I will give thanks to you, LORD, among the nations, and will sing praises to your name.

ends.sectionTitle: The Weak and the Strong; Paul’s Plans and Greetings
ends.excerpt: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, “Therefore I will give praise to you among the Gentiles and sing to your name.”

connections.label: I will be his father
connections.explanation: In the promise to David, God says of David's offspring that he will be his father and the heir will be his son. Hebrews quotes the words, with a line from Psalm 2, to show that God speaks of the Son as he never spoke of any angel.

ends.excerpt: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the children of men;

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?” and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”

connections.label: One of his line on his throne
connections.explanation: God promises to raise up David's offspring after him and establish the throne of his kingdom forever. At Pentecost Peter says David, as a prophet, knew God had sworn to set one of his descendants on his throne, and applies it to the risen Christ; the word for throne is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.excerpt: When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will set up your offspring after you, who will proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
Therefore, being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him that of the fruit of his body, according to the flesh, he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,

connections.label: Elijah prayed and it did not rain
connections.explanation: Elijah tells Ahab there will be no dew or rain except at his word, and after the contest on Carmel the sky grows black and a great rain falls. James names Elijah as a man like us who prayed that it would not rain, and prayed again for rain; the word for rain is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Elijah: Drought, the Widow, and Carmel
ends.excerpt: Elijah the Tishbite, who was one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my…

ends.sectionTitle: The Tongue, Humility, the Rich, Patience and Prayer
ends.excerpt: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.

connections.label: Seven thousand who did not bow to Baal
connections.explanation: At Horeb Elijah complains that Israel has killed the prophets, thrown down the altars, and that he alone is left, and God answers that he has kept seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal. Paul quotes the exchange as what Scripture says about Elijah, to show that a remnant remains; his verb for being left is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.excerpt: He said, “I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I, even I…

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:

connections.label: The Queen of the South
connections.explanation: The queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's fame and comes to test him with hard questions, and is overwhelmed by his wisdom. Jesus says that the Queen of the South will rise in judgement against his generation: she travelled from the far ends of the world for Solomon's wisdom, and something greater than Solomon is here.

ends.sectionTitle: The Queen of Sheba; Solomon's Fall
ends.excerpt: When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the LORD’s name, she came to test him with hard questions.

ends.sectionTitle: Toward Jerusalem: the Samaritan, Martha and Mary
ends.excerpt: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one…

connections.label: Solomon built him a house
connections.explanation: Solomon builds the temple, and at its dedication he asks whether God will really dwell on earth, since heaven cannot contain him. Stephen names Solomon as the one who built God a house, then says the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands.

ends.excerpt: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, which is the second month…
But Solomon built him a house. However, the Most High doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says,

connections.label: God feeds the ravens
connections.explanation: During the drought God sends Elijah to a brook where the ravens bring him bread and meat morning and evening. Jesus tells his disciples to consider the ravens, which neither sow nor reap, yet God feeds them; his word for the ravens, found nowhere else in the New Testament, is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Elijah: Drought, the Widow, and Carmel
ends.excerpt: You shall drink from the brook. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” So he went and did according to the LORD’s word, for he went and lived by the brook Cherith that is before the Jordan.

ends.sectionTitle: Toward Jerusalem: the Samaritan, Martha and Mary
ends.excerpt: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!

connections.label: Barley loaves
connections.explanation: A man brings Elisha twenty loaves of barley, and a hundred men eat with some left over. In John's account of the feeding of the five thousand the boy's five loaves are barley loaves, and the leftover pieces fill twelve baskets; the adjective, found only here in the New Testament, is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.excerpt: A man from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give to the people, that they may…

ends.sectionTitle: Five Thousand Fed; Walking on the Sea
ends.excerpt: “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”

connections.label: They became vain
connections.explanation: Kings explains the fall of the northern kingdom: the people rejected God's covenant, followed vanity and became vain. Paul says of those who knew God but did not honour him that they became vain in their reasoning, with the Septuagint's verb, found nowhere else in the New Testament (below).

ends.excerpt: They rejected his statutes and his covenant that he made with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testified to them; and they followed vanity, and became vain, and followed the nations that…

ends.sectionTitle: The Gospel; All under Sin; Righteousness through Faith
ends.excerpt: Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened.

connections.label: A leather belt around his waist
connections.explanation: The king's messengers describe the man who met them as hairy and wearing a leather belt around his waist, and the king knows it is Elijah. Matthew describes John the Baptist's clothing of camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist, in the Septuagint's words (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Elijah's Last Acts; the Chariot of Fire
ends.excerpt: They answered him, “He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.” He said, “It’s Elijah the Tishbite.”

ends.sectionTitle: John the Baptist; the Temptation; the First Disciples
ends.excerpt: Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

connections.label: A new covenant
connections.explanation: Jeremiah announces days when the LORD will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah, writing his law on their hearts. Hebrews quotes the whole oracle and argues from it that the first covenant has been made old.

ends.excerpt: “Behold, the days come,” says the LORD, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah,

ends.sectionTitle: The New Covenant and the Once-for-All Sacrifice
ends.excerpt: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold, the days are coming”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;

connections.label: Rachel weeping for her children
connections.explanation: Jeremiah hears a voice in Ramah, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted. Matthew quotes it as spoken by Jeremiah the prophet and fulfilled when Herod killed the children of Bethlehem.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”

ends.sectionTitle: The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus
ends.excerpt: Then that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, “A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be…

connections.label: A den of robbers
connections.explanation: Standing in the gate of the temple, Jeremiah asks whether the house called by the LORD's name has become a den of robbers. Clearing the temple, Jesus says that it is written that his house is a house of prayer but they have made it a den of robbers, in the Septuagint's words (below).

ends.excerpt: Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, I myself have seen it,” says the LORD.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Teaching in the Temple
ends.excerpt: saying to them, “It is written, ‘My house is a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a ‘den of robbers’!”

connections.label: The new covenant at the supper
connections.explanation: Jeremiah promises a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Over the cup after supper Jesus calls it the new covenant in his blood, the phrase Jeremiah 31:31 introduced.

ends.excerpt: “Behold, the days come,” says the LORD, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah,

ends.sectionTitle: The Last Supper and the Arrest
ends.excerpt: Likewise, he took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.

connections.label: Let him who boasts boast in the Lord
connections.explanation: Jeremiah tells the wise, the mighty and the rich not to glory in their wisdom, strength or riches, but in knowing the LORD. Paul quotes it in short form as written, at the end of his argument that God chose the foolish things of the world; the verb is the Septuagint's (below).

ends.excerpt: The LORD says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom. Don’t let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches.

ends.sectionTitle: Divisions and the Wisdom of the Cross
ends.excerpt: that, as it is written, “He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.” When I came to you, brothers, I didn’t come with excellence of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.

connections.label: Rest for your souls
connections.explanation: Jeremiah tells the people to ask for the old paths and walk in the good way, and they will find rest for their souls. Jesus invites the weary to take his yoke and learn from him, promising rest for their souls in the same words.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

connections.label: Set apart from the womb
connections.explanation: God tells Jeremiah that before he was formed in the womb he knew him and appointed him a prophet to the nations. Paul describes his own call in similar terms, as set apart from his mother's womb and called by grace to preach among the Gentiles.

ends.excerpt: “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
But when it was the good pleasure of God, who separated me from my mother’s womb and called me through his grace,

connections.label: The potter and the clay
connections.explanation: At the potter's house Jeremiah watches a vessel remade, and the LORD says Israel is in his hand as clay in the potter's hand. Paul asks whether the potter has no right over the clay to make one vessel for honour and another for dishonour, with the Septuagint's words for potter and clay (below).

ends.sectionTitle: The Potter and the Broken Jar
ends.excerpt: The word which came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying, “Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will cause you to hear my words.”

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: But indeed, O man, who are you to reply against God? Will the thing formed ask him who formed it, “Why did you make me like this?”

connections.label: The abomination of desolation
connections.explanation: Daniel's vision of the seventy weeks speaks of one who will make the sacrifice cease and of abominations that make desolate. Jesus warns of the abomination of desolation spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place; the two Greek nouns are those of the Septuagint and Theodotion's Daniel (below).

ends.excerpt: He will make a firm covenant with many for one week. In the middle of the week he will cause the sacrifice and the offering to cease. On the wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate.…
“When, therefore, you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),

connections.label: Hair white as wool, like snow
connections.explanation: In Daniel's vision the Ancient of Days has clothing white as snow and hair like pure wool, and one like a son of man comes with the clouds. John sees one like a son of man whose head and hair are white as wool, like snow, joining the two figures of Daniel 7; the words for wool and snow are the Septuagint's (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Four Beasts and the Son of Man
ends.excerpt: “I watched until thrones were placed, and one who was Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning…
And among the lamp stands was one like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching down to his feet, and with a golden sash around his chest.

connections.label: Michael
connections.explanation: In Daniel's last visions Michael is one of the chief princes, who stands up for Daniel's people in a time of trouble. In Revelation Michael and his angels make war on the dragon; the New Testament names him only here and in Jude (below).

ends.excerpt: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; but, behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me because I remained there with the kings of Persia.

ends.sectionTitle: The Woman, the Dragon and the Beasts
ends.excerpt: There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war.

connections.label: Stopped the mouths of lions
connections.explanation: Daniel is cast into the den of lions, and in the morning he tells the king that God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths. Hebrews counts among the deeds of faith that some stopped the mouths of lions; the word for lions is the one Theodotion's Daniel uses (below).

ends.excerpt: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.”
who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked out righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

connections.label: Quenched the power of fire
connections.explanation: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image and are thrown bound into the burning fiery furnace, and come out alive. Hebrews counts among the deeds of faith that some quenched the power of fire.

ends.excerpt: Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more…
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, grew mighty in war, and caused foreign armies to flee.

connections.label: Gabriel
connections.explanation: While Daniel is praying at the time of the evening offering, the man Gabriel comes to him to give him understanding. In the temple at the hour of incense the angel tells Zechariah that he is Gabriel, who stands before God; in the New Testament only Luke names him, spelled as in the Septuagint (below).

ends.excerpt: yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

connections.label: A kingdom without end
connections.explanation: The one like a son of man is given a kingdom that will not pass away or be destroyed. Gabriel tells Mary that her son will reign forever and his kingdom will have no end, with the Septuagint's word for the kingdom (below).

ends.sectionTitle: Four Beasts and the Son of Man
ends.excerpt: Dominion was given him, with glory and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom…
and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. There will be no end to his Kingdom.” Mary said to the angel, “How can this be, seeing I am a virgin?”

connections.label: Up to half my kingdom
connections.explanation: When Esther comes before the king unbidden, he asks her request and promises it even to half his kingdom. When Herodias' daughter dances, Herod swears to give her whatever she asks, up to half his kingdom; the words are the Septuagint's in Esther 5:3 (below).

ends.excerpt: The king said, “What do you desire, Esther? What is your request? Ask even to the half of my kingdom, and it shall be yours.”

ends.sectionTitle: Rejected at Nazareth; the Twelve Sent; Five Thousand Fed
ends.excerpt: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”

connections.label: Maker of heaven, earth and sea
connections.explanation: The great prayer of Nehemiah 9 opens by confessing the LORD as maker of heaven, the earth, the seas and all that is in them. After Peter and John are released, the believers pray together to God as creator of the sky, the land and the sea and everything they hold, before asking for boldness.

ends.excerpt: You are the LORD, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve them…
When they heard it, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord and said, “O Lord, you are God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;

connections.label: Three days in the belly of the fish
connections.explanation: The LORD prepares a great fish to swallow Jonah, and he is in its belly three days and three nights. Jesus makes Jonah's three days and nights inside the fish the sign of the Son of Man's own three days and nights in the heart of the earth.

ends.sectionTitle: In the Belly of the Fish
ends.excerpt: The LORD prepared a huge fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

connections.label: Throwing the cargo overboard
connections.explanation: When the LORD sends a great storm, the sailors on Jonah's ship throw the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship. On Paul's voyage to Rome the crew, labouring in the storm, begin to throw things overboard, and Luke's word for this, found nowhere else in the New Testament, is the Septuagint's in Jonah 1:5 (below).

ends.excerpt: But the LORD sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm on the sea, so that the ship was likely to break up.
As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

connections.label: Repentance in sackcloth and ashes
connections.explanation: When Jonah preaches, the people of Nineveh fast and put on sackcloth, and their king sits in ashes. Jesus says that if his mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes; the two words are the Septuagint's in Jonah 3 (below).

ends.excerpt: The people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.

ends.sectionTitle: Toward Jerusalem: the Samaritan, Martha and Mary
ends.excerpt: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

connections.label: Asleep in the storm
connections.explanation: A great storm threatens Jonah's ship while Jonah sleeps below, and the captain wakes him to call on his God. When a storm comes down on the lake while Jesus sleeps, the disciples wake him, and he rebukes the wind and the raging water; Luke's word for the raging water, which the New Testament has only twice, is the Septuagint's for the storm in Jonah 1:4 (below).

ends.excerpt: But the LORD sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a mighty storm on the sea, so that the ship was likely to break up.
Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.

connections.label: In the spirit and power of Elijah
connections.explanation: The last words of Malachi promise that God will send Elijah the prophet before the day of the LORD, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children. Gabriel tells Zechariah that his son will go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, and takes up Malachi's words about turning hearts.

ends.excerpt: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, ‘to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children,’ and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to prepare a people prepared for the Lord.”

connections.label: He will put his angels in charge of you
connections.explanation: Psalm 91 promises the one who trusts in God that angels will guard him and bear him up so that he does not strike his foot on a stone. On the pinnacle of the temple the devil quotes the psalm as written, to tempt Jesus to throw himself down.

ends.excerpt: For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways. They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone.
for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’”

connections.label: The stone the builders rejected
connections.explanation: Psalm 118 sings of the stone the builders rejected that has become the cornerstone. After the parable of the tenants Jesus asks what this written word means, applying it to himself and to the leaders who are rejecting him.

ends.excerpt: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is the LORD’s doing. It is marvelous in our eyes.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Teaching in the Temple
ends.excerpt: But he looked at them and said, “Then what is this that is written, ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the chief cornerstone’?

connections.label: Dividing his garments
connections.explanation: In Psalm 22 the sufferer describes his enemies dividing his garments among them and casting lots for his clothing. Luke records that at the cross the soldiers divided Jesus' garments and cast lots for them.

ends.excerpt: They divide my garments among them. They cast lots for my clothing. But don’t be far off, LORD. You are my help. Hurry to help me!
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.

connections.label: The Lord said to my Lord
connections.explanation: Psalm 110 opens with the LORD telling the psalmist's lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are made his footstool. Jesus quotes it as David's own words in the book of Psalms and asks how the Christ can then be David's son.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Teaching in the Temple
ends.excerpt: David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand,

connections.label: Counted with the transgressors
connections.explanation: The fourth Servant Song ends with the servant who poured out his life to death and was counted with the transgressors. At the supper Jesus says this written word must be fulfilled in him.

ends.excerpt: Therefore I will give him a portion with the great. He will divide the plunder with the strong, because he poured out his soul to death and was counted with the transgressors; yet he bore the sins of…

ends.sectionTitle: The Last Supper and the Arrest
ends.excerpt: For I tell you that this which is written must still be fulfilled in me: ‘He was counted with transgressors.’ For that which concerns me is being fulfilled.”

connections.label: Into your hands I commit my spirit
connections.explanation: Psalm 31 is the prayer of one who trusts God in distress and commends his spirit into God's hand. Luke's last words of Jesus on the cross are this line of the psalm, addressed to the Father, before he breathes his last.

ends.excerpt: Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, LORD, God of truth. I hate those who regard lying vanities, but I trust in the LORD.
Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.

connections.label: I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh
connections.explanation: Joel promises that God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh, with sons and daughters prophesying and young and old seeing visions and dreams. At Pentecost Peter tells the crowd that this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel, and quotes the whole passage.

ends.excerpt: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
But this is what has been spoken through the prophet Joel: ‘It will be in the last days, says God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your young…

connections.label: You will not let your Holy One see decay
connections.explanation: In Psalm 16 the psalmist trusts that God will not abandon his soul to Sheol or let his holy one see corruption. Peter quotes the psalm as David's words and argues that, since David died and was buried, it speaks of the resurrection of the Christ.

ends.excerpt: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
For David says concerning him, ‘I saw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved.

connections.label: Sit at my right hand
connections.explanation: Psalm 110 has the LORD tell the psalmist's lord to sit at his right hand. Peter points out that David did not ascend to heaven, yet says this, and concludes that God has made Jesus both Lord and Christ.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
For David didn’t ascend into the heavens, but he says himself, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit by my right hand

connections.label: Heaven is my throne
connections.explanation: In Isaiah's last chapter the LORD says that heaven is his throne and the earth his footstool, and asks what house could be built for him. Stephen quotes the prophet to support his claim that the Most High does not dwell in houses made with hands.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest?
‘heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build me?’ says the Lord. ‘Or what is the place of my rest?

connections.label: Hearing but not understanding
connections.explanation: When Isaiah is sent, God tells him to say to the people that they will hear but not understand, see but not perceive. In Rome, at the very end of Acts, Paul says the Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah and quotes the commission to the leaders of the Jews, who could not agree among themselves.

ends.sectionTitle: The Song of the Vineyard; Isaiah’s Call
ends.excerpt: He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but don’t understand. You see indeed, but don’t perceive.’
When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

connections.label: Why do the nations rage?
connections.explanation: Psalm 2 asks why the nations rage and the rulers take counsel against the LORD and his Anointed. After Peter and John are let go, the believers pray, quoting the psalm as spoken by David and see it fulfilled in Herod and Pilate gathering against Jesus.

ends.excerpt: Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing? The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his Anointed, saying,
who by the mouth of your servant David, said, ‘Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?

connections.label: Rebuilding the fallen tent of David
connections.explanation: Amos ends with God's promise to raise up the fallen tent of David and rebuild its ruins, so that the nations called by his name may come. At the council in Jerusalem James quotes it as the words of the prophets to support receiving Gentile believers.

ends.excerpt: In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old,

This agrees with the words of the prophets. As it is written, ‘After these things I will return. I will again build the tabernacle of David, which has fallen. I will again build its ruins. I will set…

connections.label: Let his habitation be desolate
connections.explanation: Psalm 69 prays that the dwelling of the psalmist's persecutors be left desolate. Before Matthias is chosen, Peter quotes it as written in the book of Psalms and applies it to Judas, with a line from Psalm 109 about another taking his office.

ends.excerpt: Let their habitation be desolate. Let no one dwell in their tents. For they persecute him whom you have wounded. They tell of the sorrow of those whom you have hurt.
For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his habitation be made desolate. Let no one dwell in it;’ and, ‘Let another take his office.’

connections.label: You are my Son; today I have become your father
connections.explanation: In Psalm 2 the LORD tells his king that he is his son, begotten today. Preaching at Pisidian Antioch, Paul quotes the second psalm by name and says God has fulfilled it by raising Jesus.

ends.excerpt: I will tell of the decree: The LORD said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
that God has fulfilled this to us, their children, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm, ‘You are my Son. Today I have become your father.’

connections.label: Led as a sheep to the slaughter
connections.explanation: Isaiah describes the servant who did not open his mouth, like a lamb led to the slaughter and a sheep silent before its shearers. The Ethiopian official is reading this passage when Philip meets him, and Philip begins from it to tell him the good news of Jesus.

ends.excerpt: He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he didn’t open his mouth.
Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this, “He was led as a sheep to the slaughter. As a lamb before his shearer is silent, so he doesn’t open his mouth.

connections.label: A light for the Gentiles
connections.explanation: In the second Servant Song God says it is too small a thing for the servant to restore Israel alone: he will be a light to the nations. When the synagogue at Antioch rejects their message, Paul and Barnabas quote this as the Lord's command and turn to the Gentiles.

ends.excerpt: Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you as a light to the nations, that…
For so has the Lord commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’”

connections.label: Paul tells of his own turning
connections.explanation: Acts narrates how Saul, on the road to Damascus to arrest believers, is stopped by a light and a voice, and then preaches Jesus in Damascus. In Galatians Paul tells it himself: he persecuted the church beyond measure until God revealed his Son in him, and he returned to Damascus.

ends.excerpt: For you have heard of my way of living in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the assembly of God and ravaged it.
But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest

connections.label: Peter, the Gentiles and the circumcision party
connections.explanation: In Acts, those of the circumcision criticise Peter in Jerusalem for going in to uncircumcised men and eating with them. In Galatians Paul tells how Peter at Antioch ate with Gentiles until people came from James, and then drew back, fearing those of the circumcision.

ends.excerpt: But when Peter came to Antioch, I resisted him to his face, because he stood condemned. For before some people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when they came, he drew back and…
Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
